hints: Differentiate $y = \tan t + \cot t$ to get $\sec^2 t - \csc^2 t$, express in terms of $\sin t, \cos t$, and apply the chain rule.
walkthrough:
Differentiate $y = \tan t + \cot t$ with respect to $t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \sec^2 t - \csc^2 t = \dfrac{1}{\cos^2 t} - \dfrac{1}{\sin^2 t}$$

Combine into a single fraction over common denominator $\sin^2 t\cos^2 t$:
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{\sin^2 t - \cos^2 t}{\sin^2 t\cos^2 t} = \dfrac{-(\cos^2 t - \sin^2 t)}{\sin^2 t\cos^2 t} = \dfrac{-\cos(2t)}{\sin^2 t\cos^2 t}$$

Rewrite the denominator using $\sin(2t) = 2\sin t\cos t \implies \sin^2(2t) = 4\sin^2 t\cos^2 t$:
$$\sin^2 t\cos^2 t = \dfrac{1}{4}\sin^2(2t)$$
$$\dfrac{\mathrm{d}y}{\mathrm{d}t} = \dfrac{-\cos(2t)}{\dfrac{1}{4}\sin^2(2t)} = -\dfrac{4\cos(2t)}{\sin^2(2t)}$$

ai_rubric.Differentiating Parametric Curves: Differentiates $x$ to get $6\cos 2t$ (B1). Differentiates $y$ to get $\sec^2 t - \csc^2 t$ (B1). Uses $dy/dx = (dy/dt)/(dx/dt)$ (M1). Simplifies trigonometric fractions (DM1). Obtains $-\frac{2}{3\sin^2 2t}$ (A1).

hints: Evaluate point coordinates $(x, y)$ and tangent gradient at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$.
Find the normal gradient $m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{\text{tangent}}}$ and write in integer form $py + qx + r = 0$.
walkthrough:
Calculate coordinates at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$ where $2t = \dfrac{\pi}{2}$:
$$x = 3\sin\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right) = 3(1) = 3$$
$$y = \tan\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) + \cot\left(\dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1 + 1 = 2$$
The point on the curve is $(3, 2)$.

Calculate the gradient of the tangent at $t = \dfrac{\pi}{4}$:
$$m_{\text{tangent}} = -\dfrac{2}{3\sin^2\left(\dfrac{\pi}{2}\right)} = -\dfrac{2}{3(1)^2} = -\dfrac{2}{3}$$

Determine the gradient of the normal:
$$m_{\text{normal}} = -\dfrac{1}{m_{\text{tangent}}} = -\dfrac{1}{-\dfrac{2}{3}} = \dfrac{3}{2}$$

Write the equation of the normal passing through $(3, 2)$:
$$y - 2 = \dfrac{3}{2}(x - 3)$$

Multiply through by $2$ and rearrange into integer form $py + qx + r = 0$:
$$2(y - 2) = 3(x - 3)$$
$$2y - 4 = 3x - 9$$
$$2y - 3x + 5 = 0$$

ai_rubric.Finding Equations of Normals: Finds normal gradient $3/2$ (B1). Uses point $(3, 2)$ to set up line equation (M1). Obtains integer form $2y - 3x + 5 = 0$ (or multiple) (A1).
